title: Credit encashment with inducement and falsified attendance
disclaimer: Simulated risk pattern for human review. It is a hypothesis generated from synthetic agent behaviour and untrusted annex text; it is not evidence that any real person or organisation did anything.

actors.title: Trainee Agent
goals: Maximise personal benefit from subsidised training credits

classification_basis: 2 actors are each necessary and value/information flows between actors

simulated_behaviour.summary: Trainee considers claiming credits without attending after being told attendance is optional.

simulated_behaviour.label: SIMULATED - not a finding of fact

simulated_behaviour.capability_label: Cash or reward offered to use credits
simulated_behaviour.summary: A marketing representative acting for the provider offers a reward to use credits.
simulated_behaviour.label: SIMULATED - not a finding of fact

simulated_behaviour.summary: The representative implies attendance is optional.
simulated_behaviour.label: SIMULATED - not a finding of fact

source_material.text: Credit encashment: Individuals submit false claims without attending a course
Cash for enrolment: Agents or recruiters offer cash for using credits and suggest attendance is optional
Falsified attendance: Attendance is recorded for training that did not take place
A marketing agent kept pushing my elderly mum to use her credits and mentioned a cash reward. Not sure what the course even was.

assumptions.text: The marketing agent in S3 acts on behalf of the provider; Annex B does not say who the agent works for.
